title: Fifteen Summers and One Loose Rail
subtitle: 危险防范 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 危险防范（灾害防范·危险与防范）
meta: 主题语境：危险防范（灾害防范·危险与防范）　|　核心词汇：danger　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 danger 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the keeper ① warned of a danger that no visitor in the park would have noticed, and he said the warning was the whole of the patrol. The ② danger, meaning the risk and not the sign, ran fifteen summers and stayed unfenced; a danger, he said, is the only thing in a park that is judged by how long it is left unmarked.

Every ③ danger in that park had the same loose rail beside it, and the ④ danger at the end, meaning the one by the river and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever reported twice. A danger, his deputy said, is nine parts neglect and one part somebody willing to warn; the keeper said the warning is the part that fills fifteen summers.

The inspector meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the danger was the whole of the case, meaning the hazard on record and not the risk. The ⑥ danger, meaning the hazard on record and not any of that, is the only thing in a case that everybody files and nobody fences; danger, he said, is either something you warn of or the only word that means both a risk and a hazard. He said the hazard is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ danger had become a line in a notice, and the notice had become an argument about the loose rail. The ⑧ danger of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in July, was one park and fifteen summers of warning; danger, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to warn. She said the warning was never mentioned.

The ⑨ danger I remember is the one at the end, which was fenced in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the park. A ⑩ danger, the deputy said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being warned of; every danger, she said, is a hazard that has agreed to look like a risk. She said the hazard was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 危险；隐患（指园中实际存在的那一处）
B. n. 危险（指那份风险本身，与那块警示牌相对）
C. 固定搭配：warn of a danger 警示一处危险
D. n. 危险（指河边那一处）
E. n. 危险；风险（抽象总称，指一座园子的全部隐患）
F. n. 危险源（指通告上写到、被公示的那一处）
G. n. 危险源；危害（指记录立案的那一项）
H. n. 危险源（抽象总称，指人人归档却无人围挡的东西）

items.q: warned of a danger that no visitor in the park would have noticed
The danger, meaning the risk and not the sign
the danger was the whole of the case
The danger, meaning the hazard on record
the danger had become a line in a notice
The danger of the whole thing
A danger, the deputy said in 1978

answers.why: warn of a danger 意为“警示一处危险”，1951 年管理员警示了一处园里没有一位游客会注意到的危险。
danger 意为“危险”，指那份风险本身而不是那块警示牌，它历经十五个夏天而没有围挡。
danger 意为“危险”，指那座园子里每一处危险，每一处旁边都有同一根松动的栏杆。
danger 意为“危险”，指河边那一处，是唯一有人上报过两次的。
danger 意为“危险源、危害”，指记录立案的那一项，视察员说这个危险源就是那个案子的全部。
danger 意为“危险源”，指人人归档却无人围挡的东西而不是别的，是案子里人人都归档、却无人去围挡的东西。
danger 意为“危险源”，指通告上写到、被公示的那一处，到 1963 年这处危险成了通告里的一行。
danger 意为“危险、风险”，管理员七月写道，整件事的风险是一座园子和十五个夏天的警示。
danger 意为“危险”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1976 年被围上，至今仍被说成园里最安静的一处。
danger 为抽象总称，副手 1978 年说，一处危险是唯一会因为被警示而变得更好的东西。
